spec:
Customers want to apply a discount code to an order before they pay for it.

Add `POST /orders/:id/discount` with JSON body `{ "code": string }`.

Behaviour:
- Codes live in the existing store (`getCode` in db.ts). Matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace. The response reports the canonical code.
- A `percent` code takes `floor(subtotalCents * value / 100)` off the order. A `fixed` code takes `value` cents off. The order total can never go below 0, so a discount larger than the subtotal just brings the total to 0 (discountCents is then equal to subtotalCents).
- On success respond 200 with `{ id, subtotalCents, discountCents, totalCents, discountCode }`. The stored order must be updated too: `GET /orders/:id` shows the new discountCents/totalCents/discountCode, and paying the order afterwards charges (paidCents) the discounted total.
- An order can carry at most one discount code. Applying any code to an order that already has one (including the same code again) is a 409.
- A code with `maxRedemptions` set can be applied successfully at most that many times across all orders; after that it is a 409. Rejected requests must not change the order and must not use up a redemption.

Status codes: 401 not signed in; 404 order not found; 403 caller is not the customer who owns the order (admins cannot apply codes for customers); 400 `code` missing, not a string, or longer than 32 characters; 404 unknown or inactive code; 409 order is not `pending`; 409 order already has a discount; 409 code fully redeemed.

Support wants to refund part of an order.

Add `POST /orders/:id/refund` with JSON body `{ "amountCents": number }`.

Behaviour:
- Refundable balance = `paidCents - refundedCents`. Several partial refunds are allowed as long as the total refunded never exceeds what was paid.
- On success respond 200 with `{ id, refundedCents, refundableCents, status }` where refundedCents is the new cumulative refunded amount and refundableCents the remaining balance. The stored order is updated (`GET /orders/:id` shows the new `refundedCents`).
- When the cumulative refund reaches the full paid amount, the order's status becomes `refunded`. Otherwise status is unchanged (a shipped order stays `shipped`).
- Only the order's owner or an admin may refund.

Status codes: 401 not signed in; 404 order not found; 403 caller is neither owner nor admin; 400 `amountCents` missing or not a positive whole number of cents; 409 order status is not `paid` or `shipped` (for example `pending` or already `refunded`); 422 `amountCents` is larger than the refundable balance. A rejected request changes nothing.

Admins need to look through orders.

Add `GET /admin/orders` with optional query parameters `status`, `customerId`, `limit`, `offset`.

Behaviour:
- `status`: one of the order statuses (`pending`, `paid`, `shipped`, `cancelled`, `refunded`). `customerId`: the id of the owning user (1 to 64 characters). Both filters combine (AND).
- `limit`: whole number 1 to 100, default 20. `offset`: whole number 0 or more, default 0. Query values arrive as strings, so `"10"` is fine, but `"10.5"`, `"abc"` and `""` are not.
- Parameters not listed here are ignored.
- Respond 200 `{ total, limit, offset, orders }`. `total` is the number of orders matching the filters before paging. `orders` is the requested page, newest order first, each entry exactly `{ id, ownerId, status, totalCents, createdAt }`.
- An unknown customerId is not an error; it simply matches nothing.

Status codes: 401 not signed in; 403 caller is not an admin; 400 any invalid `status`, `customerId`, `limit` or `offset`.

Customers and support want a printable receipt for an order.

Add `GET /orders/:id/receipt`. It responds 200 with an HTML document as the body (a string) and header `content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8`.

The receipt must show:
- a heading `Receipt for order <id>`
- the customer's account name (`Customer: <name>`)
- one table row per line item with item name, quantity, unit price and line total
- the lines `Subtotal: $X.XX`, `Discount: -$X.XX`, `Total: $X.XX`, `Paid: $X.XX`, `Refunded: $X.XX` (amounts formatted as dollars with two decimals; the Discount line is always present)
- a "Ship to" block with the shipping name, line1, city, postal code and country
- `Note: <note>` when the order has a note

Only the order's owner or an admin may view the receipt. Only orders that are `paid`, `shipped` or `refunded` have one.

Status codes: 401 not signed in; 404 order not found; 403 caller is neither owner nor admin; 409 order has no receipt yet (any other status).

Customers sometimes mistype their address. Let them correct it.

Add `PATCH /orders/:id/shipping` with a JSON body containing any subset of `name`, `line1`, `city`, `postal`, `country`. The values follow the same rules that apply to the shipping address when an order is created.

Behaviour:
- Only the fields supplied are changed; the others keep their current values. Other keys in the body are ignored.
- At least one of the five fields must be present.
- If any supplied field is invalid, nothing is changed.
- Respond 200 with `{ id, shipping }` where `shipping` is the full updated address (exactly the five fields). `GET /orders/:id` shows the change.
- The address can only be changed while the order is `pending` or `paid`.
- Only the order's owner or an admin may change it.

Status codes: 401 not signed in; 404 order not found; 403 caller is neither owner nor admin; 400 body is not a JSON object, none of the five fields supplied, or any supplied field invalid; 409 order status is not `pending` or `paid`.
